answer: A jade market on a terrace could auction a fixed number of earning seats when the sun reaches its zenith. Each winner pays a nonrefundable bid; the ledger issues one key-bound permit for that epoch and consumes its serial on first use. Another alias needs another seat and payment, even for parallel colluders. Set the reserve above the maximum subsidy an added seat can earn. Security assumes an honest auction and enforceable reward ceiling; bid manipulation remains a risk. Small seat lots let newcomers bid, though prices can exclude them.
